micro_topic: Everyday chemistry > Alkali metals > Sodium storage
core_fact: Sodium is a highly reactive alkali metal: in air it reacts vigorously with oxygen (and with moisture, liberating H2, which can ignite); kerosene does not react with it and excludes air.

statements.label: opt1
statements.text: Sodium is kept in kerosene because kerosene oil is a good preservative.
statements.fact_source: NCERT Science X, ch. 3 'Metals and Non-metals' (sodium and potassium kept under kerosene)
statements.true_fact: Kerosene merely isolates Na from air; it is not a preservative in any chemical sense.

statements.label: opt2
statements.text: Sodium is kept in kerosene to prevent it from absorbing atmospheric moisture.
statements.fact_source: NCERT Science X, ch. 3 'Metals and Non-metals' (sodium and potassium kept under kerosene)
statements.true_fact: Sodium does not 'absorb' moisture; it reacts violently with water/moisture (and oxygen) – the key gives the reaction with oxygen.

statements.label: opt3
statements.text: Sodium is kept in kerosene because in open air it reacts explosively with oxygen.

phrases.meaning_here: vigorous oxidation in air, may catch fire

statements.fact_source: NCERT Science X, ch. 3 'Metals and Non-metals' (sodium and potassium kept under kerosene)

statements.label: opt4
statements.text: Sodium is kept in kerosene because it remains soft in kerosene.
statements.fact_source: NCERT Science X, ch. 3 'Metals and Non-metals' (sodium and potassium kept under kerosene)
statements.true_fact: Sodium is soft (knife-cut) by nature; softness is not the storage reason.
statements.mechanism: true fact not the one asked

reconstruction.correct_statement: Sodium is kept in kerosene because in open air it reacts explosively with oxygen.
reconstruction.transformation: Reason for storage replaced by a property (softness), a false function of kerosene or a mis-stated reaction (absorption).
reconstruction.why: Kerosene excludes oxygen and moisture, with which Na reacts vigorously.
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: Na/K under kerosene; white phosphorus under water; reason = reactivity with air, not softness or 'preservation'.

key_note: Option 2 is partly defensible (Na also reacts with moisture), but 'absorb' misdescribes it; key stands.
practice: AI-GENERATED PRACTICE (not an APPSC PYQ): 'White phosphorus is stored under water because it catches fire in air' - T.

micro_topic: Everyday chemistry > Acids > Aqua regia dissolves gold
core_fact: Aqua regia ('royal water') = conc. HCl : conc. HNO3 in 3:1; it dissolves gold (forms chloroauric acid), so gold dipped in it loses weight.

statements.label: opt1
statements.text: The 'royal water' that dissolved the gold is aqua regia.
statements.fact_source: NCERT Chemistry (Class X/XI); app notes 'Relevance of S&T to Day-to-day Life' (aqua regia 3 HCl : 1 HNO3)

statements.label: opt2
statements.text: The 'royal water' that dissolved the gold is oil of vitriol.
statements.fact_source: NCERT Chemistry (Class X/XI); app notes 'Relevance of S&T to Day-to-day Life' (aqua regia 3 HCl : 1 HNO3)
statements.true_fact: Oil of vitriol is sulphuric acid; it does not dissolve gold.

statements.label: opt3
statements.text: The 'royal water' that dissolved the gold is aqua fortis.
statements.fact_source: NCERT Chemistry (Class X/XI); app notes 'Relevance of S&T to Day-to-day Life' (aqua regia 3 HCl : 1 HNO3)
statements.true_fact: Aqua fortis (nitric acid) alone cannot dissolve gold; it is one component of aqua regia.

statements.label: opt4
statements.text: The 'royal water' that dissolved the gold is bleach solution.
statements.fact_source: NCERT Chemistry (Class X/XI); app notes 'Relevance of S&T to Day-to-day Life' (aqua regia 3 HCl : 1 HNO3)
statements.true_fact: Bleach does not dissolve gold; 'royal water' = aqua regia.

reconstruction.correct_statement: The 'royal water' that dissolved the gold is aqua regia.
reconstruction.why: 'Royal water' is the literal translation of aqua regia; only it dissolves gold.
reconstruction.micro_topic_rule: Aqua regia = regia (royal) because it dissolves the royal metal; aqua fortis = HNO3; oil of vitriol = H2SO4.

practice: AI-GENERATED PRACTICE (not an APPSC PYQ): 'Aqua regia is prepared by mixing conc. nitric and hydrochloric acids in the ratio 1:3' - T.
